classification.recommended_terminology: positive invariance of the root convex hull under the continuous Newton flow
classification.attribution: Credit Gauss--Lucas only for static critical-point containment and Nagumo for the tangent-cone positive-invariance principle. Describe the reciprocal supporting-half-plane calculation and boundary-critical rigidity as the local polynomial-specific contribution. Keep the global ODE proof ordinary rather than Lean-checked.
classification.mathematical_interest: The proof is short once the reciprocal representation is written, but the global conclusion is useful: every nonsingular descending Newton trajectory begun in the root hull remains spatially confined. The equality case at a boundary critical point closes a singular geometric loophole.
classification.reusable_scope: Univariate complex polynomials and nonsingular forward trajectories of $z'=-f/f'$, with separate branch treatment at non-root critical starts. More generally, the support calculation applies to reciprocal-sum vector fields with sources in a convex body.
classification.why_it_matters: For #1041 it permanently removes spatial escape from the list of possible failures. Any remaining obstruction must be metric or combinatorial—length, turning, multiplicity, or lobe allocation—inside the convex hull.

primary_sources.title: Über die Lage der Integralkurven gewöhnlicher Differentialgleichungen
primary_sources.author: Mitio Nagumo
primary_sources.venue: Proceedings of the Physico-Mathematical Society of Japan, third series 24 (1942), 551-559
primary_sources.exact_anchor: The paper gives the foundational tangent-direction criterion for solutions of an ordinary differential equation to remain in a closed set.
primary_sources.supports: The standard positive-invariance/viability step from inward boundary vectors to forward confinement.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The Newton reciprocal formula, root convex hull, or the boundary-critical equality case.

primary_sources.title: Gauss--Lucas theorem
primary_sources.authority: classical theorem of Gauss and Lucas
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Every zero of $f'$ lies in the convex hull of the zeros of the complex polynomial $f$.
primary_sources.supports: Static placement of polynomial critical points and the reason the root hull is the natural convex body.
primary_sources.does_not_support: Forward invariance of the continuous Newton flow or any trajectory-length statement.

mechanism_comparison.static_Gauss_Lucas: Locates critical points of $f$ inside the root hull; it says nothing about the direction of $-f/f'$ on the hull boundary.
mechanism_comparison.Nagumo_positive_invariance: Turns membership of the vector field in the tangent cone at every regular boundary point into forward invariance.
mechanism_comparison.source_specific_sign_calculation: After rotating a supporting normal, each displacement has nonnegative real part, so the reciprocal sum does too and its negated inverse has no outward component.
mechanism_comparison.boundary_critical_rigidity: Equality of the reciprocal sum at a supporting face forces every root onto that face, reducing the singular boundary case to a one-dimensional polynomial.
mechanism_comparison.metric_boundary: Convex confinement does not control arclength, turning, projection multiplicity, or the choice of a short root pair.
